proposal.blind_spot: Current per-elapsed throughputs and per-active-warp stall shares cannot separate kernel-active time from idle elapsed time (launch gaps/tail waves) nor latency-bound memory under-use from true DRAM bandwidth saturation.

rationale.sm__cycles_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustai: LOW -> idle SMs during runtime: fuse sequential launches, use persistent/grid-stride kernel, or enlarge grid to remove gaps/tails; HIGH -> GPU fully busy: attack the kernel body itself by cutting DRAM bytes (single-pass fusion, smaller dtypes) or adding memory parallelism.
rationale.smsp__warps_eligible.avg.per_cycle_activ: LOW with DRAM below peak -> latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound: raise occupancy and issue more independent loads per thread to saturate DRAM; HIGH -> schedulers already have work: skip parallelism, reduce instruction/dependency count or reduce bytes.

split.chosen_by: llm_tiebreak:It combines short-scoreboard stalls with an occupancy-saturation split (warps active vs peak sustained), which physically separates latency that low occupancy failed to hide from a true near-full-occupancy regime and should generalize better than a stall-only cut or a near-100% global-load sector-efficiency cut.
